prompt: A rack holds $10$ sensors, of which $3$ are faulty. An engineer tests $4$ sensors chosen uniformly at random without replacement. Find the probability, as a fraction, that at least one tested sensor is faulty.

rubric.text: Complement event: no faulty sensor tested

solution:
At least one faulty is the complement of none faulty (axioms).
All samples: $\binom{10}{4}=210$.
None faulty: all $4$ from the $7$ good ones, $\binom74=35$ (counting).
$P=1-35/210=1-1/6=5/6$.
hints: Count the complement instead of three separate cases.

prompt: A model uses a subset of $8$ candidate features. Feature $A$ must be included, and the subset must have exactly $3$ or exactly $4$ features. How many subsets are allowed?

why: ignored the requirement that $A$ is included: $\binom83+\binom84$
fixed $A$ but chose the other features from the wrong sizes: $\binom73+\binom74$
multiplied the two cases ($7\cdot7$) instead of adding them
counted each valid subset twice

rubric.text: Fix $A$ and choose the remaining features from $7$
Split into the two size cases with the right sizes ($2$ and $3$ more)

solution:
Fix $A$ in the subset (counting).
Size $3$: choose $2$ more from $7$: $\binom72=21$.
Size $4$: choose $3$ more from $7$: $\binom73=35$.
The cases are disjoint, so add (sets): $21+35=56$.
hints: Put $A$ in first, then count what is left to choose.

prompt: In a spam-filter log, $30\%$ of emails contain the word *free*, $20\%$ contain *winner*, and $8\%$ contain both. Find the probability, as a decimal in $0$ to $1$, that a random email contains neither word.
solution:
Union by inclusion-exclusion (axioms): $0.30+0.20-0.08=0.42$ (sets).
Neither word is the complement: $1-0.42=0.58$.
Trap: adding without subtracting the overlap gives $0.50$.
hints: Neither = complement of at least one.

prompt: Server $A$ is up with probability $0.6$ and server $B$ with probability $0.7$. Nothing is assumed about how they depend on each other. What is the smallest possible value of $P(\text{both up})$?

why: assumed independence and multiplied
took the larger-probability bound $\min(0.6,0.7)$, which is the largest possible value, not the smallest
subtracted in the wrong order: $0.7-0.6$
assumed the events could be disjoint, but $0.6+0.7>1$

solution:
$P(A\cap B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cup B)$ (axioms).
The union is at most $1$ (inequalities), so $P(A\cap B)\ge 1.3-1=0.3$.
Equality holds when the union is everything, which is feasible.
hints: The union cannot exceed $1$.

prompt: A log has $20$ lines, of which $5$ are errors. Two lines are drawn uniformly at random without replacement. Given that at least one drawn line is an error, find the probability, as a fraction, that the second line drawn is an error.

rubric.text: Condition on the event $\ge1$ error, not just on a first draw

solution:
Let $S$ = second is error, $E$ = at least one error. $S\subset E$, so $P(S\mid E)=P(S)/P(E)$ (conditional).
$P(S)=5/20=1/4$ by symmetry.
$P(E)=1-\binom{15}2/\binom{20}2=1-105/190=17/38$ (counting).
$P(S\mid E)=\frac{1/4}{17/38}=\frac{19}{34}$.
hints: Every outcome with the second line an error already has at least one error.

prompt: Three sensors fail independently, each with probability $0.2$. Given that at least one sensor failed, what is the probability that exactly one failed? Give to $3$ decimals.

why: no conditioning: $P(\text{exactly one})$ alone
$P(\text{at least one})$ reported instead of the conditional
divided by $P(\text{none})=0.512$ instead of $P(\ge1)$
reused the single-sensor failure rate

solution:
Exactly one failed implies at least one failed, so numerator is $P(\text{exactly one})=3(0.2)(0.64)=0.384$ (conditional).
$P(\ge1)=1-0.8^3=0.488$ (axioms).
Ratio $0.384/0.488\approx0.787$.
hints: Exactly one failure is a sub-event of at least one.

prompt: $20\%$ of emails are spam. Two filters flag emails independently given the true class. Each flags $90\%$ of spam and $5\%$ of legitimate email. An email is flagged by both filters. Find the probability, as a fraction, that it is spam.

rubric.text: Treat the two flags as conditionally independent: multiply likelihoods per class

solution:
Both flags given spam: $0.9^2=0.81$ (independence given class).
Both flags given legit: $0.05^2=0.0025$.
Bayes: $\frac{0.2\cdot0.81}{0.2\cdot0.81+0.8\cdot0.0025}=\frac{0.162}{0.164}=\frac{81}{82}$ (bayes).
Trap: using one flag gives only $9/11$.
hints: Multiply the likelihoods within each class before using Bayes.

prompt: A factory has three lines producing $50\%$, $30\%$, $20\%$ of output, with defect rates $2\%$, $3\%$, $5\%$ respectively. A unit is found defective. What is the probability it came from line $3$? Give to $2$ decimals.

why: prior only, ignores the defect evidence
likelihood only, not weighted by the prior
divided the line-3 term by the sum of the three defect rates instead of the weighted total
complement: probability it is not from line 3

rubric.text: Weights = prior times defect rate for each line
Total defect probability by total probability
Divide line 3 weight by the total

solution:
Joint weights (axioms): line 1 $0.5\cdot0.02=0.010$; line 2 $0.3\cdot0.03=0.009$; line 3 $0.2\cdot0.05=0.010$.
Total defective $=0.029$.
Bayes: $0.010/0.029=10/29\approx0.34$ (bayes).
hints: Weight every line by its share of output times its defect rate.

prompt: Three servers are up independently with probabilities $0.9$, $0.8$, $0.7$. The service works when at least two servers are up. Find the probability, as a fraction, that the service works.

rubric.text: List the disjoint up-patterns with at least two up

solution:
At least two up means all three, or exactly two (axioms, four disjoint patterns).
All up: $0.9\cdot0.8\cdot0.7=0.504$ (independence).
Only 3 down: $0.9\cdot0.8\cdot0.3=0.216$; only 2 down: $0.9\cdot0.2\cdot0.7=0.126$; only 1 down: $0.1\cdot0.8\cdot0.7=0.056$.
Sum $=0.902=451/500$.
hints: Enumerate which servers are down in each allowed pattern.

prompt: $X$ and $Y$ are independent fair $0/1$ bits. Let $Z=1$ exactly when $X\neq Y$, else $Z=0$. What is $P(X=1,\,Y=1,\,Z=1)$?

why: multiplied the three marginals, assuming mutual independence
used $P(X=1,Y=1)$ and ignored $Z$
used $P(Z=1)$ alone
squared the pair probability

rubric.text: Reject the product of marginals despite pairwise independence

solution:
$Z=1$ iff $X\neq Y$ (conditional).
$X=1,Y=1$ gives $Z=0$, so the triple event is impossible: probability $0$.
The three variables are pairwise independent but not mutually independent (independence), so $1/8$ is wrong.
hints: Check what $Z$ equals when both bits are $1$.

prompt: A job retries $X\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ times with $P(X=k)=c\,(k+1)$. Find $P(X\ge2\mid X\ge1)$ as a fraction.

rubric.text: Normalise the pmf to find $c$ (or work with weights)

solution:
Weights are $1,2,3,4$ for $k=0..3$, total $10$, so $c=0.1$ (discrete-rv).
$P(X\ge1)=0.9$ and $P(X\ge2)=0.7$.
$P(X\ge2\mid X\ge1)=0.7/0.9=7/9$ (conditional).
hints: The constant $c$ cancels in the ratio.

prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled and $Y=|d_1-d_2|$. What is $P(Y\ge2)$?

why: this is $P(Y\ge1)$
treated the $21$ unordered pairs as equally likely
this is $P(Y\ge3)$ (strict inequality slip)
this is $P(Y\le1)$, forgot the complement

solution:
Use ordered pairs, $36$ equally likely (counting).
$Y=0$: $6$ outcomes. $Y=1$: $2\cdot5=10$ outcomes.
$P(Y\ge2)=1-16/36=20/36=5/9$ (discrete-rv).
hints: Count the small gaps, then take the complement.
check: Fraction(sum(1 for a in range(1,7) for b in range(1,7) if abs(a-b)>=2),36)

prompt: A system logs $8$ independent failures. Each failure is one of $5$ equally likely types. Find the expected number of distinct types that appear, as a decimal.

rubric.text: Indicator variable for each type appearing
Probability a given type is missed: $(4/5)^8$

solution:
Let $I_t=1$ if type $t$ appears (expectation).
$P(I_t=0)=(4/5)^8$ because the failures are independent (independence), so $P(I_t=1)=1-(4/5)^8\approx0.832$.
By linearity: $5\cdot0.832\approx4.16$.
No joint distribution of the indicators is needed.
hints: Sum indicators, one per type.

prompt: A request is retried until it succeeds; each attempt succeeds independently with probability $1/4$. The system gives up after $3$ attempts. Let $N$ = number of attempts made (at most $3$). What is $E[N]$?

why: uncapped geometric mean $1/p$
the cap itself, assuming all attempts are always used
dropped the $P(G\ge3)$ term in the tail sum
summed the tail one term too far (cap of $4$)

rubric.text: Model attempts as geometric with $p=1/4$ and cap at $3$

solution:
$N=\min(G,3)$ with $G$ geometric on $1,2,\dots$ (discrete-dists).
$E[N]=\sum_{k=1}^{3}P(G\ge k)$ (expectation).
$P(G\ge k)=(3/4)^{k-1}$: $1+3/4+9/16=37/16$.
hints: For a nonnegative integer variable, add the tail probabilities.

prompt: Let $A\sim\text{Poisson}(4)$ and $B\sim\text{Binomial}(12,\,0.25)$ be independent. Find $\text{Var}(3A-2B+5)$.

rubric.text: Scale by squared coefficients; the constant adds nothing

solution:
$\text{Var}(A)=4$ (Poisson); $\text{Var}(B)=12(0.25)(0.75)=2.25$ (discrete-dists).
$\text{Var}(aX+c)=a^2\text{Var}(X)$, and the $-2$ is squared (variance).
Independent, so $9\cdot4+4\cdot2.25=36+9=45$.
hints: Coefficients enter squared; the shift drops out.

prompt: A team runs $20$ independent hypothesis tests where every null hypothesis is true. Each test has a $0.05$ chance of a false positive. Find the probability, as a decimal in $0$ to $1$, of at least $2$ false positives.
hints: Subtract the two smallest outcomes from $1$.

prompt: Server errors arrive as a Poisson process with rate $3$ per hour. What is the probability of no errors in a given 20-minute window and at least one error in the 40 minutes right after it?

why: used the hourly rate in both windows without rescaling
used the wrong length for the second window (20 minutes again)
only asked for at least one error in the full hour
only asked for no errors in the full hour

rubric.text: Rescale the rate: mean $1$ for 20 min, $2$ for 40 min

solution:
Counts in disjoint windows are independent (independence).
20 min: mean $3\cdot\frac13=1$, so $P(0)=e^{-1}$ (discrete-dists).
40 min: mean $2$, so $P(\ge1)=1-e^{-2}$.
Product: $e^{-1}(1-e^{-2})\approx0.318$ (exp-log).
hints: Scale the rate to each window length first.

prompt: A response time $X$ (seconds) has density $f(x)=c(1+x)$ on $[0,2]$ and $0$ elsewhere. Find $P(X>1)$ as a fraction.
solution:
$\int_0^2(1+x)\,dx=2+2=4$, so $c=1/4$ (pdf-cdf).
$P(X>1)=\frac14\int_1^2(1+x)\,dx=\frac14\left(1+\frac32\right)$ (integral).
$=\frac{5}{8}$.
hints: Normalise first, then integrate the tail.

prompt: A service time $X$ has CDF $F(x)=x^2/4$ on $[0,2]$. What is $E[X]$?

why: used $F$ as if it were the density
the upper end of the support
used $f(x)=x$ (dropped the $1/2$), unnormalised
the median, not the mean

solution:
$f(x)=F'(x)=x/2$ on $[0,2]$ (pdf-cdf).
$E[X]=\int_0^2 x\cdot\frac x2\,dx$ (expectation).
$=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{8}{3}=\frac43$ (integral).
hints: The CDF is not the density.

prompt: Two independent latencies are $X_1\sim N(200,\,40^2)$ and $X_2\sim N(100,\,30^2)$ in ms. Find $P(X_1+X_2>350)$, as a decimal in $0$ to $1$.

rubric.text: Standardise: $z=1$ and take the upper tail

solution:
Sum of independent normals is normal (normal, independence).
Mean $300$; variance $40^2+30^2=2500$, so sd $50$ (variance).
$z=(350-300)/50=1$.
$P(Z>1)=0.1587$.
Trap: adding sds gives $70$.
hints: Variances add for independent variables, sds do not.

prompt: Scores are normal. $10\%$ of scores fall below $40$ and $20\%$ fall above $70$. Use $z_{0.90}=1.2816$ and $z_{0.80}=0.8416$. What is the standard deviation, to $1$ decimal?

why: rounded both $z$ values to $1$ and added them
divided the $30$ gap by the lower-cutoff $z$ only
divided the $30$ gap by the upper-cutoff $z$ only
subtracted the $z$ values instead of adding

rubric.text: Convert each tail to a $z$ value, with the lower one negative

solution:
Lower: $(40-\mu)/\sigma=-1.2816$. Upper: $(70-\mu)/\sigma=+0.8416$ (normal).
Subtract to remove $\mu$: $30=(0.8416+1.2816)\sigma$.
$\sigma=30/2.1232\approx14.1$ (variance).
hints: Two equations, two unknowns; subtract to cancel the mean.

prompt: Two machines fail independently. Each has an exponential lifetime with mean $50$ hours. Both have already run $30$ hours without failing. Find the probability, as a decimal in $0$ to $1$, that both survive at least $20$ more hours.

rubric.text: Memoryless property removes the $30$ hours already run

solution:
Exponential is memoryless, so the past $30$ hours do not matter (conditional, cont-dists).
One machine: $P(T>20)=e^{-20/50}=e^{-0.4}$.
Independent machines (independence): $e^{-0.4}\cdot e^{-0.4}=e^{-0.8}\approx0.449$.
hints: The past survival does not change the remaining-life distribution.

Region $|X-Y|\ge2$ is two right triangles with legs $8$

prompt: Binary features $X,Y$ have joint pmf: $P(0,0)=0.4$, $P(0,1)=0.1$, $P(1,0)=0.2$, $P(1,1)=0.3$. Find $\text{Var}(X+Y)$ as a fraction.
hints: Variances alone are not enough; add twice the covariance.

prompt: $\text{Var}(X)=4$, $\text{Var}(Y)=9$ and the correlation of $X$ and $Y$ is $-0.5$. What is $\text{Var}(2X-Y)$?

why: flipped the sign of the cross term
ignored the covariance entirely
subtracted $\text{Var}(Y)$ for the $-Y$ term: $16-9$
used cross term $ab\,\text{Cov}$ without the factor $2$

solution:
$\text{Cov}=\rho\sigma_X\sigma_Y=-0.5\cdot2\cdot3=-3$ (joint-cov).
$\text{Var}(2X-Y)=4\cdot4+1\cdot9+2(2)(-1)(-3)$ (variance).
$=16+9+12=37$.
hints: The cross term is $2ab\,\text{Cov}$ with $b=-1$.

prompt: Daily error counts have mean $20$ and standard deviation $4$ (distribution unknown). Use Chebyshev's inequality to bound $P(X\ge30\ \text{or}\ X\le10)$. Give the bound as a fraction.
solution:
The two tails together are $|X-20|\ge10$ (tail-bounds).
Chebyshev: $\sigma^2/t^2=16/100$ (variance).
$=4/25$.
Trap: Markov on $X\ge30$ gives $2/3$ and ignores the variance.
hints: Two-sided deviation of $10$ from the mean.

prompt: A conversion rate $p$ is unknown. The sample proportion $\hat p$ comes from $n$ independent users. Using Chebyshev with the worst-case variance of a Bernoulli, what is the smallest $n$ that guarantees $P(|\hat p-p|\ge0.05)\le0.05$?

why: used variance $1$ instead of the worst case $1/4$
dropped the $0.05$ failure probability
did not square the tolerance $0.05$
doubled for a two-sided event that Chebyshev already covers

solution:
$E[\hat p]=p$ and $\text{Var}(\hat p)=p(1-p)/n\le1/(4n)$ (expectation, variance).
Chebyshev (tail-bounds): $P\le\frac{1}{4n\varepsilon^2}$ with $\varepsilon=0.05$.
The bound is $100/n$, so $100/n\le0.05$ gives $n\ge2000$.
hints: Worst-case Bernoulli variance is $1/4$.

prompt: Session lengths are independent with mean $8$ min and sd $6$ min. For $100$ sessions, use the CLT to estimate the probability, as a decimal in $0$ to $1$, that the total exceeds $900$ min.
solution:
Sum of $100$ iid terms is approximately normal (lln-clt).
Mean $=800$; sd $=6\sqrt{100}=60$ (normal).
$z=(900-800)/60\approx1.667$.
$P(Z>1.667)\approx0.048$.
hints: Sum of $n$ terms has sd $\sigma\sqrt n$.

prompt: A true conversion rate is $p=0.2$. With $n=400$ independent users, use the CLT (no continuity correction) to estimate $P(|\hat p-0.2|<0.02)$. Give to $3$ decimals.

why: took the standard error as $0.2/\sqrt{400}=0.01$, using $p$ not $\sqrt{p(1-p)}$
used one-sided $\Phi(1)$
tail probability outside the band
used $\Phi(1)-\Phi(0)$, one side of the band

solution:
Bernoulli sd is $\sqrt{0.2\cdot0.8}=0.4$, so $SE=0.4/\sqrt{400}=0.02$ (lln-clt).
The band is $\pm1$ SE, so $z=1$ (normal).
$P(|Z|<1)\approx0.683$ (discrete-dists for the Bernoulli sd).
hints: Compute the Bernoulli sd before dividing by $\sqrt n$.
